chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Bellhops and Hot Chocolates uniforms; dances and fairs
summary: Coleman first called the band the Bellhops, then Hot Chocolates; they played fairs and dances around Norfolk and Richmond.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: band, hot -- first he had a band called the Bellhops, and they wore little bell caps, and little vests like bellmen wear. And I was in on that band, and I wore that stuff once.

Then he changed the name to the Hot Chocolates and he got some almost identical kind of suits where they had brown suits with a stripe down the pants, little vests, and the stripe down the pants, a white shirt, and a brown bow tie. That's all they wore. That was the Hot Chocolates. That was that band, yeah. And he used to travel. We'd go to Norfolk, and Richmond, all the little places around out of Washington, and play, you know.
Did you play mostly dances or --

Oh, that's all we played. Played fairs, and dances, and things like this. Little country fairs and dances. That's all we played, yeah. That's all we played. Most bands then were dance bands. Most all the bands around at that particular time were dance bands. The first show band I ever worked in was that Hardy Brothers band, because Tommy Miles really wasn't a show band. It was more of a swing and dance band, you know.
